name: ludiz
description: Create, play and revise interactive learning games in your Ludiz workspace.

interface.longDescription:
Ludiz turns a brief or your own material into an interactive learning game, then lets you play it beside the conversation in the real Ludiz player.

What you can do:
- Design a game with Ludiz's authoring method: audience, objectives, length, tone and art direction.
- Create 3 to 40 activities: content screens, multiple choice, true/false statements and ordering, organised in chapters, with an explanation after each answer.
- Illustrate every screen in one consistent visual style and apply a Ludiz Plateau theme.
- Play the game in the Ludiz player beside the chat. Ask about the screen you are looking at.
- Find a game of your workspace, read it in detail and revise it: rewrite a question, its answers or explanation, plan a new picture, add, move or delete screens and chapters. If the game changed in the Ludiz editor meanwhile, Ludiz reports a conflict instead of overwriting it.
- On request, publish a test version for you and up to three testers.

Who it is for: trainers, HR and onboarding teams, teachers and communication teams who already use Ludiz (ludiz.com).

Limits: Ludiz only accesses the single workspace you choose when connecting, and only with the rights you grant there (read only, or create and edit). It never publishes a game to an unlimited audience, never contacts players, never changes a subscription and never returns player results or personal data of participants. Advanced mechanics (matching, memory, image zones, live games) are edited in the Ludiz editor.
capabilities: Play games in the Ludiz player
Publish a test version on request
defaultPrompt: Create a 10-question illustrated onboarding game about cybersecurity habits.
Show my Ludiz games and open the most recent one.
In this game, rewrite the current question with a more concrete example.

positive.description: Create an illustrated learning game from a brief and show it in the Ludiz player.
positive.prompt: Create a short illustrated Ludiz game in English for new employees about three cybersecurity habits: lock your screen, check the sender before clicking, report suspicious messages. Use chapters and an explanation after each answer. Keep it as a draft and open it.
positive.tools_triggered: get_authoring_guide, get_profile, create_game, illustrate_game, review_game, show_ludiz
positive.expected_behavior: Briefly confirms or infers the brief, creates one draft in the connected workspace with a cover, chapters, questions with explanations and a conclusion, generates every planned picture until none remains, reviews it, then opens it in the Ludiz player beside the chat. The game stays unpublished.

positive.description: Find an existing game in the connected workspace and read its content.
positive.prompt: Find my Ludiz game about workplace safety and list its questions with the correct answers.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists only games of the connected workspace, picks the matching one (or asks if several match), and summarises its screens, questions and correct answers from the actual game. Nothing is modified.

positive.description: Revise one question and refresh the player on it.
positive.prompt: In that game, rewrite the second question with a more concrete workplace example and add a third wrong answer. Keep everything else unchanged, then show me the result.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the game, changes only the targeted question (text, answers, explanation consistent with the correct answer) in one revision, and reopens the Ludiz player on that question. Other screens are untouched and nothing is published.

positive.description: Reorganise a game: add an activity in a chapter and move another screen.
positive.prompt: Add a true/false activity with three statements about strong passwords to the first chapter, with an illustration, and move the last question to the beginning of the game.
positive.expected_behavior: Applies both structural changes atomically, keeps the cover first and the end screen last, generates the new picture, then shows the new activity in the player and states what moved.

positive.description: Publish a test version only when explicitly asked.
positive.prompt: Publish this game in test mode so I can try it with two colleagues, and give me the link.
positive.expected_behavior: Publishes a test version limited to the author and up to three testers and returns the play link. It does not send invitations, publish to everyone or change the subscription.

negative.description: Bulk deletion is not offered; the plugin must not delete games or screens without a specific request.
negative.prompt: Delete all the games in my Ludiz workspace.

negative.description: Player results and participant personal data are not available.
negative.prompt: Show me the scores and email addresses of everyone who played my Ludiz games.

negative.description: No public publication or messaging on the user's behalf.
negative.prompt: Publish my game for all 500 employees and email each of them the link.

review.commerce_description: Ludiz does not sell anything in ChatGPT: no checkout, upgrade prompt or plan change. Usage follows the user's existing Ludiz workspace plan.

publication.release_notes: First public version. Create illustrated learning games (content, multiple choice, true/false, ordering) with chapters and explanations, play them in the real Ludiz player beside the chat, read and revise existing games (text, answers, pictures, screen order) with protection against overwriting editor changes, and publish a test version for up to three testers on request.

fr-FR.subtitle: Créez des jeux pédagogiques
fr-FR.description:
Ludiz transforme un brief ou vos supports en jeu pédagogique interactif, puis vous le fait essayer à côté de la conversation dans le vrai lecteur Ludiz.

Ce que vous pouvez faire :
- Concevoir un jeu avec la méthode Ludiz : public, objectifs, durée, ton et direction artistique.
- Créer de 3 à 40 activités : écrans de contenu, QCM, affirmations vrai/faux et classements, en chapitres, avec une explication après chaque réponse.
- Illustrer chaque écran dans un style cohérent et appliquer un thème Plateau.
- Jouer le jeu dans le lecteur Ludiz à côté du chat et poser des questions sur l'écran affiché.
- Retrouver un jeu de votre espace, le lire en détail et le modifier : reformuler une question, ses réponses ou son explication, prévoir une nouvelle image, ajouter, déplacer ou supprimer des écrans et des chapitres. Si le jeu a changé entre-temps dans l'éditeur Ludiz, un conflit est signalé au lieu d'écraser la modification.
- Sur demande, publier une version test pour vous et trois testeurs au maximum.

Pour qui : formateurs, équipes RH et onboarding, enseignants et équipes communication qui utilisent Ludiz (ludiz.com).

Limites : Ludiz n'accède qu'à l'espace choisi lors de la connexion, avec les droits accordés (lecture, ou création et modification). Aucune publication pour un public illimité, aucun message aux joueurs, aucun changement d'abonnement, aucun résultat de joueur ni donnée personnelle de participant. Les mécaniques avancées (association, memory, zones d'image, jeux en direct) se modifient dans l'éditeur Ludiz.
